machine.split.memory0Max.note: Machines page, Settings tab, Memory split (advanced): the warning under the split's fields when memory 0 is too large (Save waits). {{max}}: the most memory 0 holds, MiB.

machine.split.nodes.message: at most {{max}} NUMA nodes past memory 0
machine.split.nodes.note: Machines page, Settings tab, Memory split (advanced): the warning under the split's fields when it lists too many NUMA nodes (Save waits). {{max}}: the most NUMA nodes (8).

machine.split.node.message: a NUMA node holds 1 to {{max}} MiB (not {{mib}})

machine.numa_one.message: {{fast}} MiB of it is the machine's fast memory; the guest gets the other {{rest}} MiB as a second NUMA node, slower to reach (each access goes through the emulator's slow path), which Linux uses once the first node is full.
machine.numa_one.note: Warning under the RAM choice (Machines page, Settings tab; the toolbar's Machine menu) when the RAM goes past memory 0 into one NUMA node. {{fast}}: memory 0's MiB; {{rest}}: the MiB past it.

machine.numa_other.message: {{fast}} MiB of it is the machine's fast memory; the guest gets the other {{rest}} MiB as {{count}} more NUMA nodes, slower to reach (each access goes through the emulator's slow path), which Linux uses once the first node is full.
machine.numa_other.note: Warning under the RAM choice (Machines page, Settings tab; the toolbar's Machine menu) when the RAM goes past memory 0 into several NUMA nodes. {{fast}}: memory 0's MiB; {{rest}}: the MiB past it; {{count}}: how many NUMA nodes past memory 0.

machines.ramdiskName.note: The name a new ramdisk gets when the user gives none (Machines page, Disks tab, Add a disk). Stored: it stays the disk's name.

machines.storage.machine.note: An item of What takes it, the list of what fills the browser's storage (Machines page, at the bottom), before its size (MachinesPage.storage.item). {{name}}: a machine, whose firmware variables and snapshots these are.

definitions.notJson.message: this file isn't a machine definition (it isn't JSON)
definitions.notJson.note: Error headline in the Machines page's message bar after Import a definition…: the file chosen isn't JSON.

definitions.notDefinition.message: this file isn't a machine definition
definitions.notDefinition.note: Error headline in the Machines page's message bar after Import a definition…: the file is JSON, but not a machine definition.

definitions.version.message: this definition is version {{version}}; this page reads version {{reads}}
definitions.version.note: Error headline in the Machines page's message bar after Import a definition…: a definition of another version. {{version}}: the file's; {{reads}}: the one this page reads.

definitions.damaged.message: this machine definition is damaged (a field is missing or out of range)
definitions.damaged.note: Error headline in the Machines page's message bar after Import a definition…: a field is missing or out of range.

store.diskAttached.message: the disk is attached to {{machines}}: detach it first
store.diskAttached.note: Error headline in the Machines page's message bar when the user deletes a disk some machines still have. {{machines}}: their names, comma-separated.

urlcheck.corsHint.message: CORS for this page's origin: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` (this origin or *), `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Content-Range, Content-Length, ETag`, and `Range` allowed in answers to OPTIONS
urlcheck.corsHint.note: What a server must send for CORS, placed in the URL problems urlcheck.noAnswer and urlcheck.noPiece. Header names in backquotes stay as they are.

urlcheck.notUrl.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Machines page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: what was typed isn't a URL.

urlcheck.https.message: The URL must be HTTPS: the page is served securely and the browser blocks plain HTTP from it.
urlcheck.https.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Machines page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: a plain HTTP URL on another origin.

urlcheck.httpOnly.message: Only http(s) URLs can be disks.
urlcheck.httpOnly.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Machines page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: a URL of another scheme (ftp:, file:…).

urlcheck.noAnswer.message: The server didn't answer the page, or answered without CORS. It needs {{needs}}.
urlcheck.noAnswer.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Machines page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: the request failed (the network, or CORS: the browser doesn't say which). {{needs}}: urlcheck.corsHint.

urlcheck.notFound.message: The server says there is no such file (404).
urlcheck.notFound.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Machines page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: the server answered 404 (for the image, or a chunked image's manifest).

urlcheck.noRanges.message: The server ignores byte ranges (it sent the whole file for a range request): it must answer `Range: bytes=…` with 206 Partial Content.
urlcheck.noRanges.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Machines page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: the server answered a range request with the whole file (200).

urlcheck.rangeStatus.message: The server answered {{status}} {{statusText}} to a range request (it should be 206).
urlcheck.rangeStatus.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Machines page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. {{status}}: the HTTP status code; {{statusText}}: the server's text for it.

urlcheck.hiddenRange.message: The server sends Content-Range but the page can't see it: it needs `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Content-Range`.
urlcheck.hiddenRange.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Machines page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: the range was answered, but CORS hides its Content-Range header.

urlcheck.suffixStatus.message: The server answered {{status}} to a suffix range (`bytes=-512`); it should be 206.
urlcheck.suffixStatus.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Machines page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. {{status}}: the HTTP status code of a request for the file's last bytes.

urlcheck.preflight.message: The server refused a preflighted range request: its answer to OPTIONS must allow the `Range` header (`Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Range`).
urlcheck.preflight.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Machines page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: the CORS preflight of a suffix range failed.

urlcheck.manifestStatus.message: The server answered {{status}} {{statusText}} for the manifest.
urlcheck.manifestStatus.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Machines page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: a chunked image's manifest. {{status}}: the HTTP status code; {{statusText}}: the server's text for it.

urlcheck.badManifest.message: The manifest isn't a chunked image's: {{why}}.
urlcheck.badManifest.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Machines page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: the manifest (JSON) was read, but isn't a chunked image's. {{why}}: what's wrong with it (a message of its own).

urlcheck.pieceStatus.message: The server answered {{status}} {{statusText}} for the image's first piece (it should be next to the manifest, as tools/chunk-image.ts wrote it).
urlcheck.pieceStatus.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Machines page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: a chunked image's first piece. {{status}}: the HTTP status code; {{statusText}}: the server's text for it. The tool's path stays as it is.

urlcheck.noPiece.message: The server didn't give the page the image's first piece. It needs {{needs}}, for the pieces too.
urlcheck.noPiece.note: A problem with a disk's URL, in the list Add a disk shows under the URL after checking it (Machines page, Disks tab), and in the error when the URL is added anyway. Here: the request for a chunked image's first piece failed. {{needs}}: urlcheck.corsHint.

urlcheck.slow.message: The first boot reads it over the network, and what it read stays in this browser, so the next boots read that from here. A chunked image with a boot's reads in its manifest (tools/disk-trace.ts) first-boots about as fast as a file. To keep all of it, store it in the browser.
urlcheck.slow.note: Note beside a URL disk (Machines page, Disks tab) and after a URL checks out in Add a disk: how a disk over the network is read. The tool's path stays as it is.

MachinesPage.state.running.note: Machines page: a machine's state, in the list of machines (after its disks) and beside its name at the top of its pane. Here: it runs (in this tab or another).

MachinesPage.state.suspended.note: Machines page: a machine's state, in the list of machines (after its disks) and beside its name at the top of its pane. Here: it has a suspended copy (Start resumes it).

MachinesPage.state.off.note: Machines page: a machine's state, in the list of machines (after its disks) and beside its name at the top of its pane. Here: it is off.

MachinesPage.otherTab.message: It runs in another tab: power it off there first.
MachinesPage.otherTab.note: Machines page: message bar text (also an error headline) when an edit that needs a machine off finds it running in another tab.

MachinesPage.powerOff.confirm.message: Power {{name}} off? Like pulling the plug: unsaved work in the guest is lost.
MachinesPage.powerOff.confirm.note: Machines page: confirmation dialog's text before an edit that needs the machine on this page off (e.g. on the Disks tab). {{name}}: the machine.

MachinesPage.powerOff.ok.note: Machines page: the confirm button of MachinesPage.powerOff.confirm's dialog.

MachinesPage.busy.saving.note: Machines page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: Save on the Settings tab, or a Connect at start box.

MachinesPage.orphans.confirm.message: This change orphans its snapshots: they were taken of a machine with the old settings (they stay, marked, until deleted).
MachinesPage.orphans.confirm.note: Machines page, Settings tab: confirmation dialog's text when Save changes the machine's shape and it has snapshots.

MachinesPage.clockSync.note.message: Snapshot and Suspend first press the guest's sleep key, so the guest suspends itself (as a laptop does when its lid closes) and is woken once the file is written; loading the file wakes it the same way, so its clock catches up with the time the file sat. A guest that doesn't sleep on the key (no systemd-logind) is saved as it is, after waiting up to 10 s. Off, a snapshot is a pause the guest can hardly tell, and its clock lags until something sets it.

MachinesPage.keyboard.followNote.note: Machines page, Settings tab: note under the Keyboard layout menu when it is This browser's, at every boot, and the browser reports no layout now. "Don't set it" quotes the menu's first option.

MachinesPage.keyboard.setNote.message: The next time the machine boots, the page changes the guest's own keyboard settings to this layout (console, X11 and Wayland, on a guest with systemd 256 or newer), and again at every boot while it is set. "Don't set it" leaves the last layout set.
MachinesPage.keyboard.setNote.note: Machines page, Settings tab: note under the Keyboard layout menu when a layout is chosen. "Don't set it" quotes the menu's first option.

MachinesPage.shape.note.message: vCPUs, RAM, the display and Vulkan, the network adapters, the USB controller, the mouse, the touchscreen, the clock device and shared folders make the machine's shape: changing one orphans the snapshots taken before (they stay, marked, until deleted). The JIT cache doesn't: the guest doesn't see it.
MachinesPage.shape.note.note: Machines page, Settings tab: the note at the tab's bottom, under Save.

MachinesPage.adapter.note: Machines page, Network tab: the name of each network adapter. {{n}}: its place, from 1.

MachinesPage.adapter.mac.note: Machines page, Network tab: the line under an adapter's name. {{mac}}: its MAC address.

MachinesPage.adapter.connection.note: Machines page, Network tab: the adapter's connection, under its name. {{name}}: the connection's name; {{kind}}: what it is (a MachinesPage.connection kind). The connection's state and MachinesPage.adapter.primary may follow, after a " · ".

MachinesPage.adapter.noConnection.message: No connection: the cable is out
MachinesPage.adapter.noConnection.note: Machines page, Network tab: in place of the adapter's connection when it has none.

MachinesPage.adapter.primary.note: Machines page, Network tab: after an adapter's connection (after a " · ") when it is the one the guest's default route goes through.

MachinesPage.adapter.atStart.title.message: Connect it when the machine starts (Disconnect turns it off)
MachinesPage.adapter.atStart.title.note: Machines page, Network tab: tooltip of Connect at start.

MachinesPage.adapter.atStart.note: Machines page, Network tab: the label of a box on an adapter with a connection.

MachinesPage.adapter.attach.title.message: A connection of this browser's, or a new one
MachinesPage.adapter.attach.title.note: Machines page, Network tab: tooltip of Attach… and Change connection….

MachinesPage.adapter.change.note: Machines page, Network tab: button on an adapter with a connection that opens the connection wizard to pick another.

MachinesPage.adapter.attach.note: Machines page, Network tab: button on an adapter without a connection that opens the connection wizard.

MachinesPage.busy.detaching.note: Machines page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: an adapter's Detach.

MachinesPage.adapter.detach.title.message: Take the connection off the adapter (its client stops)
MachinesPage.adapter.detach.title.note: Machines page, Network tab: tooltip of Detach.

MachinesPage.adapter.detach.note: Machines page, Network tab: button on an adapter with a connection that takes it off.

MachinesPage.busy.disconnecting.note: Machines page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: an adapter's Disconnect.

MachinesPage.adapter.disconnect.note: Machines page, Network tab: button on an adapter of the machine running on this page while its connection is up.

MachinesPage.busy.connecting.note: Machines page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: an adapter's Connect.

MachinesPage.adapter.connect.note: Machines page, Network tab: button on an adapter of the machine running on this page while its connection is down.

MachinesPage.adapter.saveFirst.note: Machines page, Network tab: on an adapter added but not saved yet, in place of its buttons.

MachinesPage.adapter.remove.title.message: Take the adapter out (the machine restarts without it)
MachinesPage.adapter.remove.title.note: Machines page, Network tab: tooltip of Remove.

MachinesPage.adapter.remove.note: Machines page, Network tab: button on each adapter that takes it out of the machine.

MachinesPage.adapters.none.message: No network adapters: the machine is offline.
MachinesPage.adapters.none.note: Machines page, Network tab: in place of the list when the machine has no adapter.

MachinesPage.adapters.add.note: Machines page, Network tab: button under the list of adapters.

MachinesPage.adapters.note.message: Up to {{max}}, each with its own MAC (eth0, eth1… in the guest, in this order). Adding, removing or moving one changes the machine's shape: snapshots taken before are orphaned. A connection is attached, changed or detached while the machine runs, as a cable is; the guest's default route goes through the first adapter that reaches the internet.
MachinesPage.adapters.note.note: Machines page, Network tab: the note under the list of adapters. {{max}}: the most adapters (4).

MachinesPage.netConfig.title.message: At every boot the page has the guest's systemd-networkd take what each connection's lease says
MachinesPage.netConfig.title.note: Machines page, Network tab: tooltip of Take the connection's settings in the guest.

MachinesPage.netConfig.message: Take the connection's settings in the guest
MachinesPage.netConfig.note: Machines page, Network tab: the label of a box under the adapters.

MachinesPage.netConfig.on.message: At every boot the page has the guest's systemd-networkd take each connection's MTU (a tailnet's is 1280: at the adapter's 1500, large packets can be lost) and search domain (MagicDNS's), and use DHCP on adapters nothing else sets up, on a guest with systemd 256 or newer. Nothing is written to the guest's disk: it lasts until the guest shuts down. NetworkManager takes them by itself.
MachinesPage.netConfig.on.note: Machines page, Network tab: the note under Take the connection's settings in the guest, while it is ticked.

MachinesPage.netConfig.off.message: The page leaves the guest's network settings alone: the guest takes the MTU and search domain only if it is set up to. The next boot has none of the page's settings.
MachinesPage.netConfig.off.note: Machines page, Network tab: the note under Take the connection's settings in the guest, while it is unticked.

MachinesPage.shares.title.message: One virtio-9p device through which the guest reaches this machine's folders: the guest sees it, so turning it on or off changes the machine's shape
MachinesPage.shares.title.note: Machines page, Shared folders tab: tooltip of the Shared folders box.

MachinesPage.shares.note: Machines page, Shared folders tab: the label of the box that gives the machine the shared folders device.

MachinesPage.shares.orphans.on.message: Turning shared folders on changes the machine's shape: the snapshots taken before are orphaned (they stay, marked, until deleted), as a RAM change does.
MachinesPage.shares.orphans.on.note: Machines page, Shared folders tab: warning under the Shared folders box once it is ticked (not saved yet).

MachinesPage.shares.orphans.off.message: Turning shared folders off changes the machine's shape: the snapshots taken before are orphaned (they stay, marked, until deleted), as a RAM change does.
MachinesPage.shares.orphans.off.note: Machines page, Shared folders tab: warning under the Shared folders box once it is unticked (not saved yet).

MachinesPage.sharesMount.title.message: At every boot the page has the guest's systemd mount the device, at the first access
MachinesPage.sharesMount.title.note: Machines page, Shared folders tab: tooltip of Mount shared folders in the guest.

MachinesPage.sharesMount.message: Mount shared folders in the guest
MachinesPage.sharesMount.note: Machines page, Shared folders tab: the label of a box under Shared folders.

MachinesPage.sharesPath.note: Machines page, Shared folders tab: the label of the field with the path where the guest mounts the shared folders.

MachinesPage.sharesPath.noteRunning.message: Mounting over a directory that has files hides them. A new mount point takes effect at the next start. On a guest with systemd 256 or newer; nothing is written to its disk.
MachinesPage.sharesPath.noteRunning.note: Machines page, Shared folders tab: the note under Mount point, while the machine runs on this page.

MachinesPage.sharesPath.note.message: Mounting over a directory that has files hides them. On a guest with systemd 256 or newer; nothing is written to its disk.
MachinesPage.sharesPath.note.note: Machines page, Shared folders tab: the note under Mount point.

MachinesPage.empty.message: Choose a machine, or make a new one.
MachinesPage.empty.note: Machines page: in place of a machine's pane when none is chosen.

MachinesPage.storage.persisted.message: The browser's storage: {{used, bytes}} used of {{quota, bytes}}, kept under pressure.
MachinesPage.storage.persisted.note: Machines page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. Here: the browser keeps it when space runs short. {{used}}: the bytes the page uses; {{quota}}: the most it may.

MachinesPage.storage.message: The browser's storage: {{used, bytes}} used of {{quota, bytes}}.
MachinesPage.storage.note: Machines page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. {{used}}: the bytes the page uses; {{quota}}: the most it may.

MachinesPage.busy.asking.note: Machines page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: Keep it under pressure (the browser is asked).

MachinesPage.storage.persist.note: Machines page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. A button that asks the browser to keep the page's storage when space runs short.

MachinesPage.storage.clear.title.message: Remote disks read again from the network (a running machine too, from now on). Kept a week after their last use at most; the browser may also take them back when space runs short
MachinesPage.storage.clear.title.note: Machines page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. Tooltip of Clear remote disks' blocks.

MachinesPage.busy.clearing.note: Machines page: what the page is doing, shown in the top bar (MachinesPage.busy) while an action runs. Here: Clear remote disks' blocks.

MachinesPage.storage.clear.note: Machines page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. A button that drops the kept blocks of URL disks. {{size}}: their bytes.

MachinesPage.storage.items.note: Machines page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. The summary of a folded list of what fills the storage.

MachinesPage.storage.item.note: Machines page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. An item of What takes it. {{what}}: what (a machines.storage.* message); {{size}}: its bytes.
